A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 25 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v9 reports original language-model training experiments, including optimizer comparisons using test loss, iterations, and runtime in Section 6 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v10 retains these original experiments, including the 450M-parameter Llama3 comparison against SOAP and Muon in Figure 9.

M1.justification: The optimizer updates and algorithm descriptions, including Figures 3 and 12, are unchanged. The new short-sided Muon connection is a theoretical special case, not a revision to the proposed practical algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same language-model evaluations on FineWeb, C4, and OpenWebText, including the tensor-valued NanoMoE setting and the larger Llama3 experiment in Appendix H.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the experiments. In particular, Muon already appears alongside SOAP in Figure 9 of v9; its expanded theoretical discussion in v10 does not add an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain the same model configurations, data quantities, batch sizes, precision settings, decomposition frequencies, and hyperparameter-search procedures, including 150 search runs and Figure 9's 120 runs per method.

E4.justification: The grafting comparison, eigenvalue-EMA ablation, and Frobenius/VN variant analyses in Figures 2, 4, 5, 7, 10, and 11 are unchanged. The new Muon passage adds no empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Random-search reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides additional repeated-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance testing relative to the other.

E6.justification: The empirical curves, table entries, and reported findings are unchanged. Figure 9 still reports KL-Shampoo outperforming Muon per iteration but performing worse against wall-clock time.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds an explicit equivalence between short-sided KL preconditioning and momentum-free scaled Muon, with scaling sqrt(max(d_a,d_b)). It also addresses the opposite matrix orientation and specifies a pseudoinverse interpretation for rank-deficient gradients. Existing numbered claims and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about the KL framework, improved structured estimation, competitive training performance, runtime, and memory advantages.

C2.justification: The new Section 3.2 passage explains that KL minimization produces matrix-shape-dependent scaling and connects this to using a global step size across weight matrices. v9 distinguished statistical whitening from Muon's deterministic orthogonalization without this explicit special-case explanation.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, precision choices, initialization, damping/clipping information, and practical implementation in Figure 12 are unchanged. The new pseudoinverse qualification concerns the theoretical equivalence rather than a reported implementation change.

R1.justification: v10 supplements the contrast with Muon by identifying a restricted equivalence to scaled Muon and citing Liu et al. (2025) in that discussion. This refines the relationship to existing research; Liu et al. and the other bibliography entries were already present in v9.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 gains a short headed passage and a connecting phrase in the preceding paragraph. The section sequence and nearly all existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from page 6 to page 7, and Figure 3 moves from page 8 to page 9 without content changes. The addition causes text and reference reflow; experimental plots and all appendix pages remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v10 makes the special-case relationship between KL preconditioning and scaled Muon explicit, supplementing v9's distinction between their orthogonalization perspectives. The accompanying explanation of matrix-shape scaling improves conceptual clarity and research positioning. This is a limited gain, with the practical algorithms, empirical evidence, and appendix proofs unchanged.
